The finite parity classes are relatively clopen. On positive limiting masses, continuous product-test integrals converge after division by the class mass. A vanishing class contribution is bounded by its own mass times the test supremum, so weak continuity covers disappearing classes.

Adding A|x|² to any polynomial for large A makes its Hessian nonnegative on compact C. Along each segment this gives convexity, so the polynomial is the difference of two continuous convex functions. Their bounded monotone integrals converge. Stone–Weierstrass and compactness then give one weak limit for the full sequence.

Weak continuity makes the limit fixed, and the variance identity implies every positive parity has one support atom. Coordinate integrals preserve the ambient barycenter in the limit. Source 233dacf87d7f01e6:01 §1 (1)–(3) matches the class weights and all convergence conclusions.

It has the same canonical selection for finite atomic lattice laws and gives the covariance and fixed-law identity there. It does not give convergence on compact mixed sets, whose continuous conditional laws can have infinite support.

Its fixed-law theorem uses globally conditioning independent endpoints and imposes a different weighting of parities. That fixed-law criterion also requires uniform support weights in its admissible class.
